energy.hotWaterPipeR.note: IECC 2018 as amended, IDAPA 24.39.30.600.06 (read on Justia). R-3 on hot water pipes (where required: >=3/4 in, recirculating, etc.); base value from knowledge, not directly read. Confidence medium. The 2018 file had a state change here (None found.); the base has none.

struct.windSpeedBasis.note: Local input, not a model value. Boise publishes SDC C, frost 24 in, 20 psf ground snow; its page still lists wind 90 mph (basic, old format), roughly 115 Vult.

struct.windExposureDefault.note: Exposure B applies wherever Exposure C does not. C applies on open terrain with scattered obstructions under 30 ft over more than 1 mile (open flat land, shorelines); the building official decides.

struct.seismicBracingExempt.note: Seismic provisions list detached one- and two-family dwellings only in D0, D1, D2 (townhouses are covered in C), so a detached house in SDC C is braced for wind alone. Exemption exception wording not read directly; inferred from the applicability list and Table R602.10.1.3 giving SDC C spacing only for townhouses. The 2018 file had a state change here (Idaho amends R602.10 to allow R602.12 or APA SR-102 as alternatives.); the base has none.

struct.liveLoads.note: Habitable attics 30. Exterior balconies and decks 40 in the 2018 IRC (Seattle's reprint strikes the 40 and amends it to 60; that amendment does not apply in Idaho).

struct.floorDeadLoad.note: Heading of the 10 psf columns used for floors without heavy finishes; the other columns use 20 psf.

struct.joistSpans40.note: Residential living areas, 40 psf live, L/360, 10 psf dead. Source is Seattle's printing of the 2018 IRC table (no Seattle change flagged); the 2018 DF-L 2x10 at 16 in value 15-7 matches the example given. Table R502.3.1(2) is not amended by Idaho.

struct.joistBearingWood.note: Minimum end bearing on wood or metal.

struct.joistBearingConcrete.note: Minimum end bearing on masonry or concrete.

struct.joistLapOverSupport.note: Minimum lap of joists from opposite sides over a support; three 10d face nails.

struct.headersExterior.note: Ground snow 30 psf column (columns are 30, 50, 70 psf; there is no 20 psf column). Footnote says use the 30 psf column when ground snow is under 30 psf and roof live load is 20 psf or less, so it applies to Boise's 20 psf. Building width is perpendicular to the ridge; interpolation allowed. Unbraced header top: multiply 2x8-2x12 spans by 0.70. NJ of 1 may be a framing anchor. Cells were read by an extraction tool from Seattle's copy; spot-check before relying.

struct.headersInterior.note: Girder and header spans for interior bearing walls; the table has no 1-2x rows. Same footnotes as R602.7(1). Cells read by extraction tool; spot-check.

struct.headerTableSpecies.value: No. 2 grade Douglas fir-larch, hem-fir, southern pine or spruce-pine-fir (minimum properties)
struct.headerTableSpecies.note: Short paraphrase of the species footnote.

struct.headerKingStuds.unit: full-height studs each end, by max header span ft
struct.headerKingStuds.note: Column for up to 115 mph Exposure B (the other column, under 140 mph B, gives 1,2,2,3,3,3,4,4). Table is keyed by 4,6,8,10,12,14,16,18 ft spans; for spans between, use the larger. Column heading read from an extraction; verify.

struct.studSpacing.note: Bearing walls. 2x4 not permitted with two floors. Walls need sheathing on one side or bridging within 4 ft vertically. Habitable attic on 2x4 limited to 32 ft roof span.

struct.studMaxHeight.note: Maximum laterally unsupported stud height for 2x4 and 2x6 bearing walls (taller needs engineering or larger studs).

struct.soilBearing.note: Classes: crystalline bedrock; sedimentary and foliated rock; sandy gravel and gravel (GW, GP); sand, silty sand, clayey sand, silty gravel, clayey gravel (SW SP SM SC GM GC); clay, sandy clay, silty clay, clayey silt, silt (CL ML MH CH). Clay row has a footnote: a soils investigation is needed if soils below 1500 psf are likely.

struct.soilBearingDefault.note: Official decides whether a soil test is required where data suggest expansive, compressible, shifting or questionable soils; tests done by an approved agency.

struct.footingsLightFrame.note: Light-frame footing width and thickness by ground snow (20 = 20 psf roof live load or 25 psf ground snow), soil bearing, stories and foundation (basement = plain concrete basement wall). For a 32 ft wide house; the table allows 2 in of width and 1 in of depth per 4 ft of width either way. Read from a text copy of the 2021 IRC (Colorado), and the Texas, Montana and Pennsylvania copies agree cell by cell; 72 cells differ from the 2018 table.

struct.footingMinWidth.note: Smallest width anywhere in Idaho's footing table. The 2018 file had a state change here (Idaho Table R403.1); the base has none.

struct.footingMinThickness.note: Idaho text (and IRC) require footings at least 6 in thick. The 2018 file had a state change here (Idaho R403.1.1 rewrite); the base has none.

struct.footingProjectionMin.note: Projection beyond the wall face at least 2 in and not more than the footing thickness. The 2018 file had a state change here (Idaho R403.1.1 rewrite); the base has none.

struct.anchorBoltDiameter.note: Anchor bolts or approved straps giving equivalent anchorage; nut and washer each bolt; in middle third of plate width.

struct.anchorBoltEmbed.note: Into concrete or grouted masonry cells.

struct.anchorBoltSpacing.note: Maximum on center. SDC C townhouses and D0-D2 have extra rules (R403.1.6.1); not needed for a detached house in SDC C.

struct.anchorBoltFromEnd.note: One bolt within 12 in of each plate section end (and at least 7 bolt diameters from the end).

struct.anchorBoltMinPerPiece.note: At least two bolts per plate section.

struct.plainConcreteWall.section: Table R404.1.2(3) (8-inch flat basement wall, vertical reinforcement)
struct.plainConcreteWall.note: The 2018 IRC has no plain-concrete table shaped like the request: Table R404.1.2(1) is horizontal reinforcement only (one No. 4 bar near top and mid-height for 8 ft or less). Cells here come from Table R404.1.2(3) for 8-inch nominal flat walls: 'PC' stands for NR (no vertical bar required, treated as plain concrete OK); otherwise the bar size and maximum spacing in inches ('#6 @ 41'). L/240, soil classes GW/GP/SW/SP (30 psf/ft), GM/GC/SM/SM-SC/ML (45), SC/ML-CL/CL (60). No interpolation. A 10 ft wall table also exists. Wall heights 8, 9 and 10 ft (the 10 ft rows from the second check).

struct.foundationWallMinThickness.note: Prescriptive concrete wall tables start at 6 in nominal flat walls; the thickness section (R404.1.5) was not found in the sources I could read, so this is my best value.

struct.unbalancedBackfillNoDesign.note: First rows (4 ft and 5 ft backfill) need no vertical bar in the 8-inch table; Table R404.1.2(2) note f requires lateral support top and bottom before backfilling 4 ft or more.

struct.concreteStrength.note: Severe weathering. Exposed and garage/porch/steps need 5-7% air entrainment. Interior slabs on grade also 2500.

struct.slabBaseCourse.note: Base course needed below grade; exception for well-drained soils.

struct.slabVaporRetarder.note: 2021 IRC requires 10-mil vapor retarder meeting ASTM E1745 Class A, joints lapped 6 in (was 6-mil polyethylene in 2018; 2024 reverts). Confirmed by Sussex County and Sycamore 2021 changes summaries.
struct.slabVaporRetarder.resolved: Second check disagreed with the first; its source was used.

struct.woodClearanceJoists.note: Not found in sources I could read; from memory of R317.1: joists 18 in, girders 12 in above exposed ground in crawlspaces must be treated or durable. Please verify. First gather could not reach a source; the number is from the second check's reading of this source.

struct.woodClearanceGirders.note: See joist note: memory value, unverified. First gather could not reach a source; the number is from the second check's reading of this source.

struct.crawlMinClearance.note: The IRC sets no minimum crawlspace height; access and ventilation apply, and R317.1 wood clearance (18 in joists, 12 in girders) governs in practice. Not read directly. First gather could not reach a source; the number is from the second check's reading of this source.

struct.columnMinWood.note: Memory value; section not found in readable sources. 4x4 minimum wood column, 3 in diameter Schedule 40 steel. First gather could not reach a source; the number is from the second check's reading of this source.

struct.columnSteel.note: Memory value; verify against R407.3. First gather could not reach a source; the number is from the second check's reading of this source.

value.16: 24/16 span rating, 7/16 in (15/32 in 32/16 also common)

struct.floorSheathing.note: Floor span columns: 24/16 and 32/16 span 16 in, 40/20 spans 20 in (covers 19.2), 48/24 spans 24 in. 19.2 in spacing is not a printed column. The extraction lost column headers, so the mapping uses the standard panel-rating floor spans.

value.16: 24/0 span rating, 3/8 in (24/16, 7/16 in is the common choice)
value.24: 24/0 span rating, 3/8 in with edge support (24/16, 7/16 in common)

struct.roofSheathing.note: 24/0 panels are rated for 24 in roof spans with edge support (20 in unsupported). Live-load check at 25 psf roof snow not independently done. Column mapping uncertain from extraction.

struct.trussDesign.value: R802.10.1 trusses designed per ANSI/TPI 1; R802.10.2 truss design drawings delivered with trusses to the job site and approved
struct.trussDesign.note: Section numbers from the list; the chapter 8 text beyond rafter tables could not be read. First gather could not reach a source; the number is from the second check's reading of this source.

struct.trussBracing.value: R802.10.3 (truss member bracing per the design drawings / BCSI)

struct.roofUplift.value: R802.11: roof assemblies need uplift connections (hurricane ties or equivalent) from rafter/truss to wall; required uplift comes from Table R802.11 by wind speed, exposure, roof span, pitch and overhang, or from truss design drawings; deduct 0.60 dead load; plus continuous load path to foundation (R606/R403).
struct.roofUplift.note: Not read directly; uplift connectors are expected at 115 mph Vult exposure B. Verify values in Table R802.11 and on truss drawings. First gather could not reach a source; the number is from the second check's reading of this source.

struct.bracingWind.unit: ft of braced panel per braced wall line
struct.bracingWind.note: By ultimate design wind speed band (94 = under 95 mph, 139 = under 140 mph), story location and braced wall line spacing. Exposure B, 30 ft mean roof height, 10 ft eave to ridge, 10 ft walls, 2 braced wall lines; adjust with Table R602.10.3(2). The story-location order is read from the printed row order. The 115 band matches the 2018 values the app had.

struct.bracingAdjust.note: Eave-to-ridge factor depends on stories supported (roof only, plus one floor, plus two floors); 5 means under 5 ft. Factor 1.6 applies to 5 or more lines. Other factors: 0.8 for an added 800 lb hold-down at each panel, top story, for DWB/WSP etc; 0.7 for GB with 4 in edge nailing and blocked joints; 2.0 for WSP/CS-WSP with horizontal blocking (this is how the printed table reads in the handout, check wording); noGypsum 1.4 applies to methods that rely on interior finish. Source is an APA handout reproducing the table, not the code itself.

struct.bwlMaxSpacing.note: Wind-only (100 to under 140 mph) spacing limit for detached houses; seismic spacing limits (25-35 ft) do not apply to a detached house in SDC C.

struct.bwlOffset.note: Exterior walls parallel to a braced wall line may be offset up to 4 ft; interior braced walls up to 4 ft from a line through the interior.

struct.panelFromEnd.note: Each panel must start within 10 ft of each end of the braced wall line. No separate combined limit found.

struct.panelMaxSpacing.note: Adjacent panel edges along a line no more than 20 ft apart. A braced wall line over 16 ft needs two panels.

struct.panelMinLength.note: WSP min is 48 in for 8-10 ft walls (53 in at 11 ft, 58 in at 12 ft). PFH 16 in supporting roof only, 24 in supporting one story and roof. CS-WSP minimum length by adjacent clear opening height (taller opening governs); 8 ft walls have no entries above 96 in. Source is an APA handout copy of the table; the extraction flagged blank cells in the 11 and 12 ft columns, which are not requested. Verify against the code.

struct.csCornerReturn.note: No 2021 change found (24 in return panel). Not text-verified.

struct.csRequiresFullSheathing.note: Continuous sheathing methods require sheathing on all sheathable surfaces of the braced wall line including above and below openings and gable ends (my memory of R602.10.4.2; not read in a source). First gather could not reach a source; the number is from the second check's reading of this source.

struct.portalFrameNote.value: PFH (R602.10.6.2): panel at least 16 in (roof only) or 24 in (one story plus roof) wide, header span 6 to 18 ft, 3/8 in WSP nailed 3 in o.c., a 5/8 in anchor bolt plus 3500 lb hold-down at one side and a 1000 lb strap opposite; for walls up to 12 ft, portal height up to 10 ft, pony wall up to 4 ft with tension straps. CS-PF (R602.10.6.4): continuous-sheathing portal, tension strap capacity from Table R602.10.6.4 (example 1200 lbf at 115 mph Exp B).
struct.portalFrameNote.note: Summarized from APA handout; verify against the code text. CS-PF minimum width not captured.

struct.panelCredit.note: WSP counts its actual length; PFH always counts 48 in regardless of width. Only panels meeting the Table R602.10.5 minimum count at all. CS-PF credit is assumed actual length (not printed in what I read). Wall height beyond 10 ft raises minimums (11 ft: 53 in WSP, 12 ft: 58 in). PFH limited to 1 story plus roof support at 24 in.

struct.headerNonBearing.value: R602.7.4: load-bearing headers are not required in interior or exterior nonbearing walls; a single flat 2x4 may serve as the header for openings up to 8 ft wide when the distance to the nailing surface above is 24 in or less, and no cripples or blocking are needed above it.
struct.headerNonBearing.note: Short paraphrase; the section is R602.7.4 'Nonbearing walls' in the 2018 text read here.

struct.cantilevers.note: Most a floor joist can reach past the wall below when it holds up only a light-frame exterior wall and roof. Rows: joist size @ spacing (in); then ground snow load (psf, 20 means 20 or less); then roof width (ft). Null means the table does not allow it. Backspan at least 3 times the cantilever; uplift connection at the backspan support. 2021 text copy agrees with every stored cell.

struct.bracingSeismic.unit: ft of braced panel per braced wall line
struct.bracingSeismic.note: By seismic design category, story location and braced wall line length, 10 ft walls. C applies to townhouses only (detached houses in A to C brace for wind only). D2 houses over two stories must be engineered (footnote h), so D2 has no first-of-three rows. The DWB/SFB/PBS/PCP/HPS column equals GB and is left out. Same numbers in the 2018 printing.

struct.bracingSeismicAdjust.note: Story height (10 ft or less 1.0, up to 12 ft 1.2) and braced wall line spacing in D0-D2 (25 ft or less 1.0, up to 30 ft 1.2, up to 35 ft 1.4). Dead load factors are 1.0 for ordinary light-frame walls and roofs and are not applied. Read from the 2018 printing (Seattle); not confirmed for 2021.

struct.bwlMaxSpacingSeismic.note: Seismic design categories D0 to D2: 25 ft, or up to 35 ft with the Table R602.10.3(4) spacing factor, which the app applies.

struct.windLimitMph.note: The IRC wind provisions do not apply at 140 mph or more in a special wind region, or where Figure R301.2.1.1 calls for wind design; the bracing table stops under 140 mph.

struct.snowLimitPsf.note: Ground snow over 70 psf: designed by accepted engineering practice.

struct.seismicEngineerCategories.note: Seismic design category E must be designed to the IBC unless reclassified to D2 (R301.2.2.1.2).
